input: Join a local community choir this fall

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing what 'joining' means to the user — just showing up to an audition, or being an active rehearsing member by a specific date — defines where the task ends and what steps are needed.
The user's geographic location determines which specific choirs are available to them and how far they are willing to travel to rehearsals.
Many choirs charge membership dues or require purchasing music/uniforms; knowing the user's budget avoids recommending options they can't afford.
Whether the choir is for the user alone or also involves a family member (e.g., a child's youth choir) changes which types of choirs are relevant.
Community choirs vary widely — sacred vs. secular, classical vs. pop/musical theatre — and the user's genre preference narrows the search significantly.
The user's weekly availability for rehearsals (evenings, weekends, hours per week) determines which choir schedules are compatible.

Understanding the user's singing experience level (beginner vs. trained) and whether they are comfortable with auditions clarifies whether prep work — like vocal warm-up practice — needs to be part of the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Join a local community choir this fall
gold.taskDescription: Find and successfully join a local community choir in time for the upcoming fall season.

questions.title: What city or neighborhood should the choir be in?
questions.description: Identifies the user's location to scope the search to geographically accessible choirs.

questions.title: What type of music do you want to sing?
questions.description: Determines genre or style preference — e.g., classical choral, gospel, pop, musical theatre, or no strong preference — to filter choir options.

questions.title: Is this choir for you, or someone else?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the user is joining personally, helping a family member (e.g., a child) join a youth choir, or both.

questions.title: Which rehearsal days or times work for you?
questions.description: Captures weekly scheduling constraints so only choirs with compatible rehearsal times are considered.

questions.title: What is your budget for dues, music, or uniforms?
questions.description: Establishes a financial ceiling to avoid recommending choirs with costs the user cannot or will not pay.

questions.title: How would you describe your current singing experience?
questions.description: Gauges whether the user is a complete beginner, casual singer, or trained vocalist, which affects both choir selection and whether audition prep is needed.

questions.title: What does successfully joining look like to you?
questions.description: Defines the finish line — e.g., attending a first rehearsal, passing an audition, performing in a fall concert — so the plan knows when the task is done.
